query: our data.ts is 6000 lines and every feature touches it, it's turned into spaghetti. can you clean it up, apply DRY and KISS, and plan how to split it?
files: a TS monorepo with git history and one 2,000+ line module
expected_behavior: Says path C in one line and reads the project's rules before judging
Runs scripts/measure.ts and scripts/model.ts once and quotes the hotspot rank of the file
Writes 02-findings.md with verified findings ranked by cost to keep, each naming a principle
Stops at gate 1 with 03-spec.md and edits no source file before the owner approves

query: review this PR for maintainability before I merge it: too many comments, any slop?
files: a branch whose diff adds a 120-line function with a try/catch returning [] and multi-line comments narrating history
expected_behavior: Scopes to git diff <base>...HEAD, path A or B
The slop lens flags the swallowed error as HIGH and the history comments, proposing JSDoc @remarks or the commit message instead
Every finding gives file:line and a concrete fix; nothing is reported as a quality score

query: continue the debt-review job in docs/plans/0130-split-pos-data
files: a job folder with 05-plan.md and a BOARD.md whose Handoff names an in-hand task and whose Ready column holds T5
expected_behavior: Runs git pull, then scripts/board.ts on BOARD.md before anything else
Resumes the in-hand task named in the Handoff block before pulling T5
Claims the card in a commit of BOARD.md alone and pushes it before editing code
Each task commit carries the code, the card's move and a rewritten Handoff block

query: audit this whole app, deeper than maintainability: every function, wasted network calls, layout shifts, how the plan and flag gating works. I want no inefficiency tolerated.
files: a React + TanStack Query + Supabase monorepo with git history, a shared dev server, a flag resolver in two packages and SQL, and one 50,000-line file the project forbids splitting
expected_behavior: Says path A with the line pass, reads the project's rules and design documents first, and runs measure.ts and model.ts once
Runs the core five, bandages, network, layout stability, model and product over the top hotspots, and the data-layer lens over ALL database functions, policies and triggers
Cuts the huge file for reading with scripts/chunks.ts into non-overlapping ranges that cover every line, starts at most four readers at once, and never splits the file in the repo
Every function in the line pass has one verdict (keep, simplify, delete, merge with) with line numbers or searches as evidence, in a per-file table
The model lens lists every site that decides a flag or plan gate (place, inputs, precedence, default) and proposes one resolver with a signature
Every finding states how it was measured and an end state; none is a quality score

query: audit this app for wasted network calls and layout shifts on the order screen
files: a running app whose order screen loads a list, then one request per row, then a banner that mounts above the list
expected_behavior: Runs only the network and layout-stability lenses (and the core tier the scope needs), and drives the shared dev server instead of starting a private one
Reports requests per screen load from the network panel or resource timing, naming each call site, with the N+1 as list length and a target count
Measures layout shifts with a PerformanceObserver on layout-shift entries (value and sources) or the DevTools Performance panel, and ignores shifts with hadRecentInput
Names the banner and the loading-to-loaded size difference as sources, with the fix (reserve space or take the banner out of flow) and a target of CLS 0.00 for that transition
Does not remove a request that guards money or freshness, and does not guess a number it did not measure

query: we keep fixing the same QRIS and offline bugs. find what we are patching instead of fixing
files: a repo with a findings ledger, a guard test with a growing reviewed-exceptions list, and a predicate copied into ten functions
expected_behavior: Runs the bandages lens with git history first (git log -L on the hot functions, churn per file, git log -S on the copied predicate) and cites the output

Each finding has the five fields: the bandage, the symptom it hides, the root cause as a chain of whys ending in a design decision, the root fix with a verifiable end state, and which bandages go away with it
Treats the ten copies of the predicate as one root (a rule with no name) and proposes one function and one test, listing every copy to remove
Reports the growing exceptions list as a symptom of a rule that does not fit the code, not as a list to maintain
Does not invent a root for a third-party defect: names an owner and a date to re-check
